result.title: NOMAD-EEG: Native Omni-Montage Adaptive Diffusion
result.summary: Purpose. Electroencephalography (EEG) montages, channel counts and recording lengths vary widely, but most EEG foundation models are bound to the channel set and input length they were trained on. We aimed to build a generative EEG foundation model independent of the number, identity and order of electrodes and of the input length. Methods. NOMAD-EEG is a 12.0 M-parameter diffusion model that alternates state-space layers along time, without patches, with attention across electrodes identified only by their 3D scalp position. It was pre-trained on 147 h of unlabelled EEG from a single corpus and evaluated with frozen linear probes on ten datasets with 1 to 64 electrodes against seven foundation models run under one protocol, and on two unseen populations. Results. Despite its small size (12.0 M parameters against 69 M for REVE) and single pre- training corpus, NOMAD-EEG outperformed all seven foundation models on EEGMMIDB mo- tor imagery (balanced accuracy 0.442), Siena seizure detection (macro F1 0.622) and Bonn seizure detection (AUROC 0.999), had the highest accuracy of the seven compared models on TUEP epilepsy diagnosis (0.640) and, after fine-tuning, the highest \k{appa} (0.635) and weighted F1 (0.814) on TUEV event classification. It was the best of five models on P300 detection in autism with an unseen eight-electrode montage (AUROC 0.718). With only 5 of 19 electrodes, its mean AUROC fell only from 0.942 to 0.891. Conclusion. Identifying electrodes by position and modelling time without patches let one small model, pre-trained on one corpus, outperform much larger EEG foundation models on seizure detection, epileptiform event classification, epilepsy diagnosis and motor imagery.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 NOMAD-EEG：一个 12M 参数的扩散式 EEG 基础模型，用无 patch 的时间状态空间层，以及只依据 3D 头皮位置识别电极的跨电极注意力，使模型适应任意电极数量、身份、顺序和输入长度，并在冻结线性探针与少电极场景下与多个基础模型比较。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作与视觉推理主线没有直接关联，但它用位置标识无序变长通道集合、而非固定插槽，并评估通道子集下的性能退化；这可供核查 LVR 中变长或缺失视觉证据的表示，以及长度和规模泛化问题。
